paragraphs.text: [Meizhan](yancha:meizhan) is a Fujian cultivar that came from Anxi. It is also made as [rock tea](yancha:definition), though it is not one of the four famous bushes. This leaf is from the Wuyi Mountains of northern Fujian, where the bushes root among rock in cliff country. Like other rock tea, it was finished with a [charcoal roast](yancha:making) given in several rounds, with weeks or months between them, and that roast is what dries the leaf so it keeps.

It was made in 1981 and has had forty-five years to change. Rock tea [put away for ageing](yancha:ageing) is the medium to full roast kind, because the heavier the roast, the longer the tea is said to stay good. Damp is the danger in storage. It lets kept tea go green again, which is why rock tea is held sealed, dry and cool, and why a tea that has turned is sometimes roasted again at low heat, losing a little quality each time.

brewing.text: Wuyi tea is usually brewed gongfu style with water at or near the boil, about 95 to 100°C, and about 5 to 8 grams of leaf in a 100 to 120 ml gaiwan, a third to a half full. A quick rinse, poured off at once, is common. Steeps start short, about 5 to 20 seconds, and grow a few seconds longer each round, and good rock tea gives seven steeps or more. In a larger pot, use about 2 to 5 grams for 250 to 350 ml and steep two to three minutes.

notice.text: A smoother, thicker liquor with less sharpness, the roast softened and the high aroma faded.
